questions.q: Report: 'Do not pluck the flowers,' the gardener said to the children.
questions.a: 'The gardener ordered/warned the children not to pluck the flowers.' A wrong answer 'the gardener said that do not pluck' reveals the student has no imperative frame at all — they're gluing 'that' onto an infinitive, which English forbids.

questions.q: Report: 'Please help me carry this,' she said to me.
questions.a: 'She requested me to help her carry that.' 'please' → 'requested'; me→her; this→that. A wrong answer 'she asked me to please help' keeps 'please' in reported speech — pleading is a live-performance feature, it cannot survive reporting.

questions.q: Report: 'Never swim alone,' the coach said to the boys.
questions.a: 'The coach warned/advised the boys never to swim alone' (or 'not to swim alone'). A wrong answer omitting the object ('the coach warned never to swim') reveals the student doesn't know imperative reporting requires a commanded party — English demands the object slot be filled.

questions.q: Commands and requests report with 'told/ordered/requested/asked + object + ______': 'Sit down' → 'He told me to sit down.' Negatives insert 'not' before 'to': 'Don't touch' → 'He ordered me not to touch.' Polite additions (please) are captured by 'requested' and can be dropped.

Fill in the blank: Commands and requests report with 'told/ordered/requested/asked + object + to-______': 'Sit down' → 'He told me to sit down.' Negatives insert 'not' before 'to': 'Don't touch' → 'He ordered me not to touch.' Polite additions (please) are captured by 'requested' and can be dropped.
Fill in the blank: The frame is fixed: [______ verb] + [object] + [to + base verb].
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student reports commands, requests, advice, and warnings using the told/ordered/requested/advised/warned + object + (not) to-infinitive frame, choosing the reporting verb that matches the original's force.
